metaTitle: E-commerce UX Design Agency: PDP & Checkout | Designit
metaDescription: E-commerce UX design judged on revenue per visitor: discovery, search, product pages, checkout, mobile and retention, starting from a funnel audit.
h1: E-commerce design judged on revenue per visitor, not aesthetics
subtitle: Most online stores lose buyers at a few specific points, usually the product page, the cart and the first checkout step. We find which one is costing you most, then design the fix and measure it.
author: Designit
aiAnswerTargets: What has the biggest impact on e-commerce conversion?
How do you reduce checkout abandonment?

cta.heading: Which step is costing you most?
cta.body: A two-week, fixed-scope audit ranks every leak in your funnel by revenue impact against effort.

sections.heading: Where online retail actually loses money

items.title: The product page doesn't answer the objection
items.body: Sizing, materials, delivery timing, returns: shoppers leave when a specific question goes unanswered.

items.title: Checkout asks too much, too early
items.body: Account creation before guest checkout, address before shipping cost, surprise fees at the last step.

items.title: Mobile is the majority and the afterthought
items.body: Thumb reach, form input, image zoom and payment sheets decide mobile conversion.

items.title: Acquisition subsidises a leaky funnel
items.body: Fixing the funnel is almost always cheaper per order than buying more traffic.

items.title: Discovery and navigation
items.body: Category structure and filtering so shoppers reach a relevant product quickly.

items.title: Search
items.body: Search that tolerates typos and vague queries and returns useful results.

items.title: Product pages
items.body: Structured around the objections that stop purchase.

items.title: Checkout
items.body: Guest checkout, early cost transparency, fewer fields and recoverable payment failures.

items.title: Mobile
items.body: Mobile as the primary design target, not a responsive afterthought.

items.title: Retention and post-purchase
items.body: Tracking, returns and re-order experiences, consistently underinvested relative to acquisition.

items.title: Personalisation
items.body: Recommendations and content that help rather than unsettle.

items.title: Diagnose (weeks 1 to 2)
items.body: Funnel analysis and heuristic review to find and size the biggest leaks.

items.title: Prioritise
items.body: Issues scored on revenue impact against effort.

items.title: Design
items.body: The highest-impact surfaces redesigned mobile-first, with every state specified.

items.title: Measure
items.body: Against the conversion metric agreed at the start.

items.title: Why e-commerce bounce rates run high
items.body: What the number is really telling you.

items.title: How to improve website conversion rate

faq.q: What has the biggest impact on e-commerce conversion?
faq.a: In most stores, checkout and the product page dominate, and checkout usually wins: forced account creation, late shipping costs and excessive form fields are the most common and most fixable causes of abandonment. Run the diagnostic first, though; the biggest leak differs by store.

faq.q: How much can we expect conversion to improve?
faq.a: We will not quote a number before looking. The opportunity depends on where your funnel leaks and how much traffic you have; the audit sizes each leak.

faq.q: Do you work on Shopify and other platforms?
faq.a: We design for the platform you use and its constraints, so the handoff can be built without workarounds.
